text:
emma: Quick PSA 7:07 UTC: noticed client bundle increased by ~180KB gz after the chunk reorder change. Some heavy helper landed in main. Charts on low-end devices stutter now.
kai: which helper? Any diffs?
harpreet: looks like `fast-decode` and `small-zip` were hoisted into main chunk because splitpoint `widget_common` got merged. Diff: removed splitpoint `widget_common` and merged into `main` to reduce chunk count.
(release-bot): "build 2026-03-20 17:00: splitpoints updated: widget_common merged into main"
emma: we also had a prefetch routing tweak `prefetch.window_ms reduced from 2500 -> 500` which increases fetch churn. Combined with larger main chunk, first interaction stalls.
kai: ugh. Proposed immediate actions: 1) revert splitpoint merge in canary build, 2) bump prefetch.window_ms back to 2500 for canary, 3) add an experiment to lazy-load `fast-decode` in worker.
harpreet: I can cut a quick canary build with splitpoint revert. prep binary: `canary-client-2026-03-20-revert-fastdecode`
emma: let's also add a lightweight client-side metric: main_chunk_parse_time_ms histogram so we can gate future merges.
release-bot: "canary build uploaded: canary-client-2026-03-20-revert-fastdecode at 1713007801"
kai: rolling out canary to eu now. release-bot: "canary rollout started 1713007805"
harpreet: once canary is healthy we'll promote. Also we should notify product that their A/B instrumentation sampling might be driving traffic patterns that reveal these regressions.
emma: agreed. I'll flag product infra and add to the postmortem template.
kai: follow-ups: - add parse_time histogram to client telemetry - add bundle-delta check to CI (fail if main chunk > +50KB gz) - revisit splitpoint heuristics in webpack config
harpreet: created ENG-PLAT-820 (splitpoint revert PR) and ENG-PLAT-821 (bundle-delta CI check).
emma: thanks all 389
